newsitem.title: USA: Sleepy U.S. foreign crude market showing some life.
newsitem.headline: Sleepy U.S. foreign crude market showing some life.

text.p: The market for foreign crudes into the U.S. Gulf Coast was still on the sleepy side Wednesday afternoon but began showing signs of life after OPEC puts its cards on the table in Vienna, traders said.

The Brent-West Texas Intermediate/Cushing spread, under increasing pressure in recent sessions, expanded a bit to $1.23 a barrel, signaling the possibility that Brent may soon be viable for U.S. refiners to work into their slates.
Brent was heard offered at levels that buyers began to take seriously, and West African grades were also featured.

But gasoline rich Colombian Cusiana continued to be talked thinly and at levels buyers considered far too pricey, in part because state-owned Ecopetrol has not yet announced its August loading program which will likely get real talk started.
Overall, the market looked to be more active for the second half of August, leaving the question open of just how U.S. refiners would meet their needs in the early part of the month.
Some, pointing to strength in West Texas Sour/Midland markets in recent sessions, said domestic grades could pick up the slack in the near term.
But others doubted that, saying the Brent-WTI spread would blow out as refiners broke down and started facing up to a situation of increasing tightness.
"I don't think there's going to be a squeeze, but things are getting tight," said one trader.
A Brent cargo was rumored to have been sold at August WTI/Cushing minus 35 cents, but details were vague enough to call the occurance of the deal into question.

What was clear however, was that two players, one European trading house and one U.S. refiner, were offering Brent at that price and that buyers were clearly getting interested in offers at that level.
Offers on Nigerian Qua Iboe on a delivered basis were also outstanding -- one for August 1-5, the other for August 5-10, and both priced at around Dated Brent plus $1.82-$1.84, traders said.

Also, BP was still floating an early offer for one of its upcoming Cusiana cargoes in August at $1.00 under September WTI/Cushing, but other players continued to say they they would not likely generate much buying interest until about minus $1.30.
Traders were divided as to when Ecopetrol would announce its August loading program, but most thought it would be sometime this week, perhaps even by late Wednesday.

On the OPEC front, none were surprised the 11-nation group rolled over its 25.03 million barrel per day production quota at its meeting, but most doubted it could limit output and actually hold the line at the limit as it said it would.
"You hear a lot of things, but the proof is in the pudding as they say," said one crude trader, referring to the OPEC pledge to control quota busting.

More pressing was the question of when Iraq might begin the second round of the UN-Iraq oil-for-food deal, with traders saying any delays beyond mid to late July in the resumption could push the Brent-WTI arbitrage window wide open and jump start the still subdued August market.
-- Oliver Ludwig New York Oil Desk 1 212 859 1633
